football.notes: Covers association football (soccer). Any text starting 'UNVERIFIED' was not confirmed on a fetched page (search snippet, secondary summary or our own coaching heuristic). 'DERIVED' means our own arithmetic on verified numbers.

benchmarks.label: Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1
benchmarks.howToTest: Cones at 0, 5 and 25 m (the 20 m shuttle lane plus a 5 m recovery zone). Run 20 m out and back to the beeps, then 10 s active recovery walking/jogging around the 5 m cone. Starts at 10 km/h and speeds up by level. Two consecutive missed lines ends the test; score = last completed shuttle, total distance = shuttles x 40 m. Test fresh (48-72 h after hard training).

benchmarks.label: 20 m multistage fitness test (beep test)
benchmarks.howToTest: 20 m lane, continuous running to beeps; starts at 8.0-8.5 km/h and rises ~0.5 km/h about every minute. Miss the line by >2 m twice and the test ends. Record the last level.shuttle reached. Not interchangeable with Yo-Yo scores.

benchmarks.label: 30 m sprint
benchmarks.howToTest: Standing (split-stance) start, 0.5-1 m behind the start line, all-out to 30 m. Best of 2-3 trials with 3-5 min rest between trials. Timing gates preferred; hand timing over short sprints is unreliable (Haugen & Buchheit advise against manual timing). Always re-test with the same method and surface. Optional 10 m split = acceleration.

benchmarks.label: Countermovement jump (hands on hips)
benchmarks.howToTest: Hands on hips, quick dip and jump for max height, land on the same spot. Best of 3 with ~1 min rest. Phone app (flight-time) or jump mat. Keep arm-swing setting identical between tests because arm swing changes the score a lot.

benchmarks.label: Repeated sprint ability 6 x 30 m
benchmarks.howToTest: UNVERIFIED protocol (common practice): 6 x 30 m all-out sprints, each starting every 20-25 s (walk back recovery). Record total time and % decrement from best rep.

levelPlacement.method: Place by Yo-Yo IR1 distance where available (most football-specific), else beep level; use the LOWER of aerobic and speed placement for overall intensity, and each benchmark's own band for the goal block.
levelPlacement.yoyoBandsCaveat: TopEndSports states these adult bands are guidance only and not research-based.

footballReferenceValues_yoyoIR1_m.source: Bangsbo et al. 2008 as cited by TopEndSports

levelPlacement.cmjReference: Norwegian national-team athletes (force plate, hands on hips): highest group athletic sprinters 62.7 cm men / 48.4 cm women; men jump ~33% (~10 cm) higher than women. UNVERIFIED rule-of-thumb bands for trained men 50-60 average, 60-70 good, >70 excellent; trained women 35-45 average, 45-55 good, >55 excellent.
levelPlacement.sprint30mReference: UNVERIFIED: no fetched norm table for 30 m in footballers. Use the athlete's own baseline; improvement goals expressed as % of baseline.

appLevels.beginner: Yo-Yo below average or lower / beep <7 (men) or <6 (women) / <6 months structured gym training / cannot hold 30 s single-leg balance
appLevels.intermediate: Yo-Yo average-good / 6-24 months training / passes plyometric readiness checks
appLevels.advanced: Yo-Yo excellent-elite / >2 years structured strength + speed training
appLevels.ruleSource: DERIVED from bands above plus NSCA plyometric readiness criteria

seasonPhases.offSeason: NSCA preparatory period: build base conditioning so the athlete tolerates harder work later; longest phase. Strength work: hypertrophy/endurance 50-75% 1RM, 3-6 sets x 8-20, then basic strength 80-95% 1RM, 2-6 sets x 2-6. Plyometrics 2-3 days apart. Sprint: acceleration and max-velocity blocks per Haugen table.
seasonPhases.preSeason: Shift to strength/power (NSCA: 30-95% 1RM, 2-5 sets x 2-5) and raise sport-specific intensity: repeated sprints, intermittent running (Yo-Yo style), small-sided games. UNVERIFIED: Bangsbo reports Yo-Yo scores in elite players typically rise ~20-40% across pre-season while VO2max changes only a few %, so pre-season is when the Yo-Yo goal moves fastest.
seasonPhases.inSeason: Maintenance: NSCA 85-93% 1RM, 2-5 sets x 3-6. One strength session per week kept strength and 40 m sprint gains for 12 weeks in pro footballers; one session every second week lost them (Ronnestad 2011). FIFA 11+ as warm-up every training session; before matches use only the running parts. Low-volume Nordics weekly.
seasonPhases.postSeason: Active rest under 4 weeks, low intensity and volume, recreational activity and rehab (NSCA).

improvementModel.cmj: Plyometric training raised CMJ by 8.7% on average (95% CI 7.0-10.4%), CMJ with arm swing 7.5%, squat jump 4.7% (Markovic 2007, 26 studies). Typical plyometric programs run 6-10 weeks; vertical jump can improve in as little as 4 weeks (NSCA/CSCS ch.18). DERIVED weekly rate: beginner ~1.0%/wk, intermediate ~0.6%/wk, advanced ~0.3%/wk (advanced reduced because trained athletes improve less).
improvementModel.sprint: Well-trained senior athletes improve less per year than test-retest variation; world top-100 sprinters in their early 20s improved ~0.1-0.2%/yr (Haugen 2019). Typical 20 m test noise ~0.025 s (CV 0.8-1.0%, Haugen thesis, UNVERIFIED search summary). DERIVED/UNVERIFIED planning rates for 30 m time: beginner 0.4%/wk, intermediate 0.2%/wk, advanced 0.1%/wk; any target faster than ~5% of baseline flagged as 'stretch'.
improvementModel.yoyo: UNVERIFIED: ~20-40% Yo-Yo gains across an elite pre-season (Bangsbo conference abstract via search). DERIVED planning rates: beginner 4%/wk, intermediate 3%/wk, advanced 1.5%/wk of baseline distance, capped by phase (in-season = maintain).
improvementModel.beep: UNVERIFIED/DERIVED: 0.3-0.5 levels per week for beginners, 0.2 for intermediate, 0.1 for advanced.
improvementModel.minimumDetectableChange: Treat changes smaller than ~1% on sprint and ~1 cm on CMJ as noise; don't adjust plan on them (DERIVED from Haugen reliability figure).

planLengthRule.formula: gapPct = |target - current| / current x 100; weeks = ceil(gapPct / weeklyRatePct[level][benchmark]); round up to whole 4-week mesocycles (NSCA: blocks 2-6 wk, most commonly 4) where possible; insert a lighter week after every 2-3 loading weeks (Haugen: 2:1 or 3:1 load:easy).
planLengthRule.overMax: If weeks > 16, cap at 16, set an intermediate target the athlete can reach, then re-test and generate the next block.
planLengthRule.retest: Re-test benchmark every 4 weeks (end of each mesocycle) and on deload weeks; Yo-Yo 2-4x per year in real teams (pre-, mid-, post-season).
planLengthRule.phaseCap: In-season plans: target = maintain or small gains only; cap goal-block intensity at 'maintenance' and stretch length rather than raise volume.
planLengthRule.source: DERIVED from Markovic, NSCA ch.18/21, Haugen 2019

plyoFootContactsPerSession.note: When intensity rises, volume falls. Same body area not on consecutive days; 48-72 h between plyo sessions; 2-4 plyo sessions/week max. Adolescents 2-3 days recovery; masters 3-4 days and fewer, lower-intensity contacts.

volumeModel.plyoInSeason: UNVERIFIED: football studies used ~100 contacts per session x2/week for 8 weeks (Moran 2024) and recommend 140-240 jumps/week x2 sessions inside practice (Ramirez-Campillo parameters). App rule: in-season use ~50-60% of off-season contacts, 1-2 sessions/week, never MD-1.
volumeModel.plyoReadiness: Squat 1RM ~1.5 x bodyweight is the classic prerequisite (technique matters more); stand on one leg 30 s and hold single-leg half squat 30 s. Athletes >100 kg (220 lb): no depth jumps above 18 in (~45 cm). Depth jump heights 16-42 in, average 30-32 in for advanced only.

resisted.load: light <10% velocity loss, moderate 10-15%, heavy 15-30%, very heavy >30%

sprintPerSession.levelScaling: Use low end of distance/volume/rest for beginners and youth (e.g. 20 m starts with 2 min rest), high end for advanced (e.g. 40 m with 7 min). Avoid the 70-95% 'grey zone' for speed work: sprint >=95% or tempo <70%.

volumeModel.nordics: FIFA 11+ Part 2 Nordic doses: level 1 3-5 reps, level 2 7-10, level 3 12-15 (1 set inside warm-up). Petersen 2011 used a 10-week progression of 27 sessions starting at 10 reps in week 1, then a once-weekly maintenance session (UNVERIFIED search summary). UNVERIFIED: low-volume Nordics (~1-2 sets x 3-5, 1-2x/week) produced similar eccentric strength gains to high volume (Cuthbert 2020; Cholp & Zemkova 2025).
volumeModel.strength: Off-season 2-3 sessions/wk; pre-season 2-3; in-season 1 (minimum effective, Ronnestad) to 2.
volumeModel.weeklyProgression: DERIVED: raise plyo contacts or sprint metres by no more than ~10-15% week to week within a level band; deload week = ~50-60% volume, intensity kept.

weekStructure.matchDayLabels: MD = match day; MD-1 = day before; MD+1 = day after. UNVERIFIED convention used across pro football; not from a fetched source.

inSeason_1match.MD+1: Recovery: easy bike/tempo, mobility (no plyo, no sprint)
inSeason_1match.MD-4/MD-3: Main strength session (maintenance load) + short acceleration work + low-volume plyo + Nordics
inSeason_1match.MD-2: Speed: short max-velocity exposures, low volume
inSeason_1match.MD-1: Activation only: FIFA 11+ running parts, a few short strides
inSeason_1match.daysPerWeekMapping: 2 days -> MD-4 strength/speed + MD+1 recovery; 3 days -> add MD-2 speed; 4 days -> add MD-3 conditioning; 5 days -> add MD+2 light aerobic. UNVERIFIED structure; constraints from verified rules: >=48 h between high-intensity sprint days, plyo not consecutive days, at least 1 strength/week.

weekStructure.inSeason_2matches: UNVERIFIED: with two matches/week drop extra conditioning; keep one short strength session (~30 min) on the day after recovery and FIFA 11+ warm-ups only.
hardRules: No plyo or max sprint on MD-1 or MD+1
Same-area plyo never on consecutive days (NSCA)
At least one strength session per week in-season (Ronnestad)

safety: FIFA 11+ in female youth players (Soligard 2008 cluster RCT): all injuries RR 0.68, overuse RR 0.47, severe RR 0.55; the most compliant third had 35% lower injury risk than the middle third. Adherence is the lever - surface it in the app.

Programs that include Nordic hamstring exercise cut hamstring injury rate ~51% (Al Attar 2017, RR 0.49); effect cannot be separated from the rest of the program. UNVERIFIED: van Dyk 2019 (15 studies, 8,459 athletes) also RR 0.49.
Plyometric readiness gates (1.5x BW squat ideal, 30 s single-leg balance); heavy athletes (>100 kg) limited to low boxes; watch knee valgus on landings, especially adolescents.
>=48 h between maximal sprint sessions; stop sprint reps if time drops off noticeably (UNVERIFIED cut-off ~3-5%).
Treat sudden hamstring tightness, groin pain, or pain on landing as stop signals; refer to physio.
Youth: no maximal 1RM testing; emphasise technique, longer recovery between plyo days (2-3 days).

levelPlacement.gameDemands: Elite players: ~4.4 km per game average (range 2.0-6.3 km), ~44-46 jumps per game, 43-145 accelerations (1-15 high-intensity), 24-95 decelerations, average HR 150-175 bpm (Petway 2020).

seasonPhases.offSeason: NSCA basketball example: test at start and end, resistance training is highest priority plus flexibility and aerobic base. Hypertrophy then basic strength ranges as football.
seasonPhases.preSeason: NSCA basketball example: resistance training 3x/week, anaerobic conditioning and plyometrics become the highest priorities; strength/power 2-5 x 2-5.
seasonPhases.inSeason: NSCA basketball example: ~30 min resistance sessions 1-3x/week alternated with plyometrics; most time goes to skill and tactics. Basketball games already contain ~45 jumps, so count game jumps toward weekly load (DERIVED).
seasonPhases.postSeason: Active rest <4 weeks, no formal structured workouts (NSCA basketball example).

improvementModel.vertical: Markovic: CMJ +8.7%, CMJ with arm swing +7.5% average from plyometric programs. UNVERIFIED: basketball-specific meta-analysis (Frontiers 2026) CMJ effect g = 0.77 with no significant effect of program length. DERIVED rates as football: beginner 1.0%/wk, intermediate 0.6%/wk, advanced 0.3%/wk; >10% total gap flagged 'stretch' for advanced.

planLengthRule.overMax: Cap at 16 weeks, set intermediate target, re-test.
planLengthRule.retest: Every 4 weeks; vertical can show change in ~4 weeks.
planLengthRule.phaseCap: In-season: maintain or small gains; deduct game jumps from plyo budget.

volumeModel.gameJumpCredit: DERIVED: a game counts as ~45 contacts of high-intensity jumping (Petway 2020 jump counts); in-season plyo sessions = level budget minus recent game/practice jumps, minimum 30 quality contacts.
volumeModel.sprint: Use Haugen acceleration row (10-30 m, >98%, 2-4 min rest, 100-200 m/session) - basketball sprints are short; max-velocity work optional.
volumeModel.codDecel: UNVERIFIED: progress deceleration/cut drills 2x/week off-season; elite training sessions contain ~324 changes of direction (Svilar via Petway) so in-season extra COD work is usually unnecessary.
volumeModel.strength: Off-season 2-3/week; pre-season 3/week; in-season 1-3 short (~30 min) sessions.

1-3 x 30 min lifting, alternate with plyo (NSCA)

boxing.notes: Covers boxing and striking combat sports. Fetched evidence is amateur 3x3-min data; professional (up to 12 x 3 min) prescriptions are extrapolated and marked UNVERIFIED.

benchmarks.label: Rounds sustained at target pace (bag or pads)
benchmarks.howToTest: UNVERIFIED app protocol: 3-min rounds on the heavy bag at a set work rate (e.g. RPE 8 / HR >=90% HRmax), 1 min rest; count rounds completed before pace or form drops (RPE 10 or a set punch-count drop). Retest every 4 weeks.

benchmarks.label: Punches per 3-min round
benchmarks.howToTest: UNVERIFIED: punch tracker or video count of one max-effort bag round.

benchmarks.label: Beep test
benchmarks.howToTest: As football.

benchmarks.label: 3 km run (roadwork)
benchmarks.howToTest: UNVERIFIED: flat course, best effort.

benchmarks.label: Countermovement jump
benchmarks.howToTest: As football.

levelPlacement.method: Place by rounds sustained + beep level + training age. Beginner: <3 rounds at pace; intermediate: 3-6; advanced: 6+ (DERIVED app bands, UNVERIFIED).
levelPlacement.demands: Highly trained amateurs in 3x3-min fights: HR >93% HRmax rounds 1-2, >97% round 3; lactate ~15 mmol/L (12-18); VO2 ~89% VO2max; energy 73% aerobic, 19% alactic, 8% glycolytic (Bruzas 2023, fetched abstract).

seasonPhases.offSeason: General preparation: aerobic base (roadwork, tempo), general strength (NSCA hypertrophy/basic strength ranges).
seasonPhases.preSeason: Fight camp: UNVERIFIED typical 8-12 weeks. Build round-based conditioning toward fight length + 1-2 extra rounds (UNVERIFIED practitioner convention), add strength-power and alactic sprint work (19% alactic contribution).
seasonPhases.inSeason: Fight week / taper: Haugen general power-sport taper guidance 2-3 weeks with 40-60% volume reduction, intensity maintained (applied by analogy - UNVERIFIED for boxing).

improvementModel.rounds: UNVERIFIED/DERIVED: add ~1 round at target pace every 1-2 weeks for beginners, every 2-3 weeks intermediate, every 3-4 weeks advanced. Target '12 rounds' from a beginner baseline triggers max length + intermediate milestone.

planLengthRule.formula: roundsGap = target - current; weeks = ceil(roundsGap x weeksPerRound[level]) where weeksPerRound = beginner 1.5, intermediate 2.5, advanced 3.5 (DERIVED/UNVERIFIED). Round up to 4-week blocks with a deload every 3rd-4th week.
planLengthRule.overMax: Cap at 16 weeks (UNVERIFIED typical camp 8-12 weeks); set milestone e.g. 6 rounds, then re-test.
planLengthRule.phaseCap: Final 2 weeks before a fight = taper, no new rounds added.

volumeModel.roundStructure: Train in 3-min rounds with 1-min rest to match competition; amateur bouts are 3 x 3 min; professional fights 4-12 rounds (UNVERIFIED search summary).
volumeModel.intervals: Bout data supports HIIT above ~90% VO2max for boxers (Thomson & Lamb 2017 via search summary, UNVERIFIED). App dose: 2-3 conditioning sessions/week off-season, 3-4 in camp, each 4-12 rounds by level (DERIVED).
volumeModel.alactic: Short max efforts 5-10 s with long rest (Haugen acceleration row: >98%, 2-7 min rest) to train the alactic system.
volumeModel.plyo: NSCA contacts by level; upper-body plyo (med-ball, plyo push-ups) counted separately, ~half the lower-body budget (DERIVED).
volumeModel.strength: 2 sessions/week off-season and camp; 1 in fight week -2; none in final week (UNVERIFIED).

weekStructure.fightCamp: UNVERIFIED: keep >=48 h between the two hardest sessions (rounds + sprint); hardest sparring/rounds day early in week, strength the day after, roadwork/recovery between.

sessionTemplates.name: Round-based conditioning
sessionTemplates.useWhen: Goal: last X rounds. 2-4x/week depending on phase.

exercises.name: Within-round bursts (10 s all-out every 30 s)

sessionTemplates.name: Strength + rotational power
sessionTemplates.useWhen: 2x/week off-season and camp.

sessionTemplates.name: Alactic sprints
sessionTemplates.useWhen: 1x/week off-season and camp.

sessionTemplates.name: Aerobic roadwork
sessionTemplates.useWhen: Base building; 73% aerobic contribution in bouts.

safety: Bouts drive HR >93-97% HRmax and lactate up to 18 mmol/L - screen for heart conditions; beginners build aerobic base before max-round tests.
Monitor internal load (RPE) to avoid overreaching (El-Ashker 2018, via search summary - UNVERIFIED).
Hand wraps/gloves for all bag work; stop with wrist/hand pain.
Head contact (sparring) is outside app scope; app plans cover conditioning only. Any concussion symptoms = no training until cleared.
Weight cutting is not prescribed by the app.

golf.notes: Golf plans focus on clubhead speed, rotation/mobility and back health. TPI material is case-study/marketing, not peer-reviewed.

benchmarks.label: Driver clubhead speed
benchmarks.howToTest: Launch monitor or radar (Trackman, PRGR, etc.). After warm-up, 5-10 full-effort swings, record the average of the best 3 (UNVERIFIED averaging rule). Same device each test. Each +1 mph can add up to ~3 yards (Trackman).

benchmarks.label: TPI pelvic rotation test
benchmarks.howToTest: Golf posture, arms crossed on chest; rotate the pelvis without moving the upper body. Checks lower-body rotation and separation from the upper body.

benchmarks.label: TPI torso rotation test
benchmarks.howToTest: Golf posture; rotate the upper body while keeping the pelvis still. Failing (extending the spine instead of rotating) linked to reverse spine angle and limited shoulder turn in the TPI case study.

benchmarks.label: TPI seated trunk rotation
benchmarks.howToTest: Seated (removes hips), club across chest, rotate each way; UNVERIFIED pass threshold ~45 degrees each side.

benchmarks.label: TPI pelvic tilt test
benchmarks.howToTest: Golf posture; tilt pelvis forward and back. Failure can be stability/coordination rather than mobility.

benchmarks.label: Single-leg balance
benchmarks.howToTest: Eyes open then eyes closed, each leg; TPI case golfer went from 2-3 s to 30+ s eyes open.

benchmarks.label: Seated or standing rotational med-ball throw
benchmarks.howToTest: UNVERIFIED protocol: 2-3 kg ball, side-on, throw each side, best of 3.

levelPlacement.method: Place by driver CHS against handicap norms + screen results (any failed rotation test -> start with corrective block).

appLevels.beginner: Male CHS <90 / female <75 mph or any failed screen (DERIVED)

seasonPhases.offSeason: Main window for gains: corrective mobility/stability for failed screens, then strength 3x/week for 8-10 weeks, then speed/overspeed work (TPI case-study sequence).
seasonPhases.preSeason: Shift to golf-specific high-velocity work; UNVERIFIED: 8-week programs combining general strength with golf-specific high-velocity movements, 3-4 sets of 5-15 reps, gave the best CHS gains (Uthoff 2021 review).
seasonPhases.inSeason: Maintenance strength 1-2x/week, mobility daily, speed work short; potentiation warm-ups before rounds (UNVERIFIED: bodyweight jumps/explosive warm-ups raised CHS acutely as much as speed sticks; SuperSpeed warm-up +2.6 mph faded after walking a hole).

improvementModel.chs: UNVERIFIED (Uthoff 2021 abstract via search): combined general + golf-specific training ~+4.1% CHS, general strength alone ~+1.6%, typically over ~8 weeks. DERIVED weekly rates: beginner 0.5%/wk, intermediate 0.35%/wk, advanced 0.2%/wk. TPI case study (fetched): 70-year-old went 90 -> 107 mph peak over a multi-phase program (~3 mph in first month from corrective work alone) - an outlier, not a planning rate.
improvementModel.mobility: Screens re-checked every 4 weeks; TPI case: backswing rotation 60 -> 80 degrees and hip-shoulder separation 20 -> 41 degrees within 1 month.

planLengthRule.formula: gapPct = (targetCHS - currentCHS)/currentCHS x 100; weeks = ceil(gapPct / weeklyRate[level]); if any rotation screen fails, prepend a 4-week corrective block. Round to 4-week blocks.
planLengthRule.overMax: Gap >~6% for intermediates/advanced is a stretch; cap at 16 weeks with an intermediate target.
planLengthRule.phaseCap: In-season: maintain CHS; short speed sessions only.

volumeModel.speedSwings: UNVERIFIED: overspeed/speed-stick sessions 3x/week of short sets with full rest are common practice; no multi-week RCT fetched supporting lasting gains from overspeed alone.
volumeModel.strength: 3x/week in the strength phase (TPI case), 3-4 sets x 5-15 reps for golf-specific high-velocity drills (UNVERIFIED, Uthoff).
volumeModel.plyo: Low lower-body contacts (beginner band 80-100 max); rotational med-ball throws counted as ~30-60 throws/session (DERIVED/UNVERIFIED).
volumeModel.mobility: Daily 10-min rotation/hip mobility for failed screens (UNVERIFIED dose).

weekStructure.inSeason: UNVERIFIED: 1-2 strength sessions not the day before a competitive round; potentiation warm-up (jumps + med-ball) before rounds; mobility daily.

sessionTemplates.name: Rotation correctives (TPI screen fails)
sessionTemplates.useWhen: Any failed pelvic/torso rotation, pelvic tilt or balance test; first 4 weeks.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling torso rotation with club (hips still)
Cat-cow / pelvic tilt in golf posture

sessionTemplates.name: Golf strength
sessionTemplates.useWhen: Strength phase 3x/week for 8-10 weeks (TPI case), in-season 1-2x.

sessionTemplates.name: Rotational power + speed swings
sessionTemplates.useWhen: Goal: more clubhead speed; after correctives/strength base. 2-3x/week.

exercises.name: Speed swings (light / normal / heavy stick or flipped club)
exercises.intensity: max intent, full rest; UNVERIFIED protocol

sessionTemplates.name: Pre-round potentiation warm-up
sessionTemplates.useWhen: Before range session or round.

safety: Low back pain is common; corrective work first - in the TPI case it removed the golfer's back pain within a month.
Swinging harder can cost distance through poor contact; track ball speed/strike, not CHS alone (Trackman coach note).
Screens' predictive validity is debated (Sportsmith critique via search) - use them to choose correctives, not to diagnose.
Older golfers: masters plyo rules (fewer contacts, 3-4 days recovery).
Stop rotational work with sharp back, rib or elbow pain.
